title: God Provides a Lamb
subtitle: Abraham walked up a mountain with a question — and God answered it Himself
mainTruth: God provides the offering Himself. Someone else stands in the place we could not stand.
illustrationPrompt: A ram caught by its horns in a thicket of thorn bushes on a rocky mountain top, morning light striking it, an empty stone altar nearby, two small figures further down the slope, painterly gouache illustration on parchment paper, warm stone and thorn-brown palette with one shaft of gold light, storybook quality referencing Jesus Storybook Bible by Jago, NOT cartoon, relief and provision, no violence --ar 16:9 --style raw

read.title: Read Together
read.text:
Isaac grew up — the promised boy, the child Abraham had waited a lifetime for, the son the whole promise depended on.

Then God asked Abraham to do the hardest thing anyone has ever been asked. God told him to take Isaac up a mountain and offer him there. In those days, people made offerings to God by giving something precious and laying it on an altar. And God was asking for Isaac.

We do not know everything Abraham felt that night. But early the next morning he cut the wood, saddled his donkey, and set out — because he had learned that God can be trusted, even when God does not explain.

On the way up the mountain, Isaac carried the wood himself, and he asked his father a question. 'Father — we have the fire and the wood. But where is the lamb?'

And Abraham gave the answer that this whole story is for: 'My son, God will provide Himself a lamb.'

At the top, Abraham built the altar and laid the wood. And just as he was about to obey, God called out from heaven: 'Abraham! Abraham! Do not touch the boy. Now I know that you trust Me.'

Abraham looked up. And there, caught by its horns in a thorn bush, was a ram. God had provided it. The ram was offered instead of Isaac. Isaac walked back down that mountain alive, because something else had taken his place.

Abraham named that place 'The Lord Will Provide'. And many, many years later, on a hill not far from that very spot, God kept the promise all the way. He gave His own Son as the Lamb — so that we could walk away alive.
read.childText: Isaac grew up. Then God asked Abraham to do the hardest thing ever — to take Isaac up a mountain and give him back to God. Abraham trusted God, so he went. On the way, Isaac asked, 'Father, where is the lamb?' Abraham said, 'God will provide Himself a lamb.' At the top, just as Abraham was about to obey, God called out: 'Stop! Do not touch the boy!' Abraham looked up — and there was a ram caught in a bush. God had provided it. The ram went in Isaac's place, and Isaac walked home safe. Years later God gave His own Son as the Lamb, so that we could go free too.

discuss.title: Talk About It
discuss.question: Who did God provide instead of Isaac?
discuss.parentGuide: Read this one sitting beside your child. It is the hardest story in the World and also the most important — substitution is the idea the cross cannot be understood without. Keep three things clear. God never wanted Isaac harmed and stopped it Himself. The whole story turns on Abraham's answer: God will provide the lamb, and He did. And this points straight at Jesus, who was the Lamb God provided when there was no substitute for Him. If your child is troubled, do not brush it off — say plainly, 'God stopped it. Isaac walked home. Nobody was hurt,' and let them ask again another day.
discuss.familyQuestion: Has anyone ever taken something hard for you so that you did not have to?

pray.title: Let's Pray
pray.guidedPrayer: God, thank You that You provided the lamb Yourself. Thank You that Isaac walked home safe. Thank You most of all for Jesus, the Lamb You gave for us. We could never have done it ourselves. Thank You. Amen.
pray.childPrompt: Can you thank God for giving us Jesus, the Lamb?
prayerPoints: Thank God that He provides what we cannot provide
Thank God for Jesus, the Lamb who took our place

remember.title: Remember This
remember.memoryVerse: Abraham said: 'God will give us the lamb Himself.'
remember.tip: Hold out both empty hands and say 'we have nothing' — then look up, and say: 'God will provide!' Do it three times, opening your hands wider each time.

doToday.title: Do It Today
doToday.action: Give away one thing today that you would rather keep — a snack, a turn, a favourite toy — and notice how it feels.
doToday.parentNote: This is a gentle echo, not an equivalence. The point your child can hold is that giving up something precious is real and costly, and that God gave first. Thank them specifically afterwards.
